description:
Run Python that calls Hermes tools in a loop. Use when you need 3+ tool calls with logic between them: filter or reduce large outputs before they enter context, branch, or iterate (N pages/files, retry on failure). Use normal tool calls for single calls, results you must read in full, or anything needing user interaction.

Calls share a persistent kernel: variables, imports and loaded data survive across execute_code calls; a timed-out or interrupted call loses that state.

Available via `from hermes_tools import ...` — arguments follow the tool of the same name, each returns a dict:

  web_search(query, limit=5)
  web_extract(urls, char_limit=None)
  read_file(path, offset=1, limit=2000)  # 1-indexed; returns {"content", "total_lines"}
  write_file(path, content)  # overwrites the whole file; read_file it first
  search_files(pattern, target="content", path=".", file_glob=None, limit=50)
  patch(path, old_string, new_string, replace_all=False)
  terminal(command, timeout=None, workdir=None)  # foreground only, no background/pty

Limits: 5-minute timeout, 50 tool calls per call. Stdout over 50KB shows head/tail inline; the full text is auto-saved to a file whose path rides in the result.

Scripts run in the session's working directory. Interpreter: the project's activated venv/conda python when one is active (VIRTUAL_ENV/CONDA_PREFIX — matches terminal()); otherwise Hermes's own python (the common case — stdlib plus Hermes's deps; check `import x` before relying on project packages).

Also importable: json_parse(text) — tolerant json.loads for terminal() output; shell_quote(s) — shlex.quote for dynamic shell args; retry(fn, max_attempts=3, delay=2) — exponential backoff.
name: execute_code

code.description: Python code to execute; print your final result to stdout.

reset.description: Discard the kernel's persistent state and start fresh before running this code.
